Apple's stock price rose to $345.34 after the market opened today, surpassing the $344.57 record set in July. Here's the full report.

Apple Shares Hit All-Time High

Despite Tim Cook appearing poised to hand the reins over to John Ternus while Apple's valuation sits at historic highs, last quarter's results rattled investors and sent shares tumbling roughly 10%.

Volatility persisted, though Apple clawed back some ground over the following weeks. On the day Cook handed over, Apple closed at $316.85 with a market cap of approximately $4.68 trillion.

Shortly after Ternus took the helm, Apple shares dropped as much as 3% ahead of its 'Surprise and Shine' event. Historically, Apple's stock has tended to react somewhat negatively to its September product events, yet this year the reception from both Wall Street and the general public has been overwhelmingly positive.

Today, Apple shares climbed around 1% after the open to $345.34, briefly eclipsing the previous all-time high of $344.57. As of this article's publication, Apple was trading at $341.80.

While it remains difficult to credit this rally entirely to Ternus, Apple shares have steadily climbed over the three weeks since he assumed the CEO role, reflecting investor optimism about the leadership transition and the company's current trajectory.
